data.name: FmSummary
data.value:
Fieldmatics is a multi-tenant SaaS platform for growers. It collects sensor data from greenhouses, gardens, fields and olive groves, stores it, and shows current values and history for every location. Next, it will act on that data through rules, alerts and automated irrigation.

I am designing and building it from scratch as my own product: a modular monolith on .NET 10, where sensors of any kind publish over MQTT, readings flow reliably through RabbitMQ into PostgreSQL, and growers see everything in a Blazor app.

data.name: FmTagline
data.value: An agricultural IoT platform that turns sensor readings from any hardware into clear, per-location insight for growers.

data.name: FmBusinessIntro
data.value: Growers manage environments such as greenhouses, gardens, fields and olive groves. They want to know what is happening in each one (temperature, humidity, soil moisture) and, eventually, have the system react for them. Most IoT tools are built around hardware. Fieldmatics is built around the places where things grow.

data.name: FmHlLocationText
data.value: A grower opens Greenhouse 1 and sees its current temperature, humidity and soil moisture, then the history charts. Nobody needs to know which board sent the data.

data.name: FmHlAgnosticText
data.value: An Arduino prototype today; ESP32, LoRaWAN, Modbus and third-party feeds later. Each technology plugs in through its own adapter, so the core never changes.

data.name: FmHlSaasText
data.value: Every customer account's data is isolated on the server. Ownership is derived from the data itself and is never taken from a client or device.

data.name: FmHlAutomationText
data.value: The platform grows in steps: monitoring first, then calibration, offline detection, rules and alerts, and finally automated irrigation with a fail-safe design.

data.name: FmJourneyIntro
data.value: Follow one reading, an air temperature of 23.8 °C in Greenhouse 1, from the sensor that measures it to the chart a grower looks at.

data.name: FmStep1Text
data.value: A sensor at one of your locations, for example Greenhouse 1, measures what it is built for: air temperature, humidity, soil moisture and more.

data.name: FmStep1Tech
data.value: Today the sensors are wired to an Arduino board. ESP32, LoRaWAN and Modbus devices can follow.

data.name: FmStep2Text
data.value: A small program next to the hardware, the adapter, reads the values, turns them into the standard Fieldmatics message and publishes it. Fieldmatics never needs to know which hardware they came from.

data.name: FmStep2Tech
data.value: A .NET adapter reads the Arduino over USB serial and publishes over MQTT. Every new kind of hardware gets its own adapter.

data.name: FmStep3Text
data.value: The message arrives at the Fieldmatics mailbox for hardware, which accepts messages from every publisher at any time.

data.name: FmStep3Tech
data.value: An Eclipse Mosquitto MQTT broker. Each publisher sends to its own topic.

data.name: FmStep4Text
data.value: A receiver collects every message and puts it in an internal queue. If the next step is busy or restarting, messages wait in line instead of getting lost.

data.name: FmStep4Tech
data.value: The Ingestion service forwards each message to a durable RabbitMQ queue. It never writes to the database itself.

data.name: FmStep5Text
data.value: The worker takes messages one at a time and matches every value to the right sensor, and through it to the right location and customer. A message leaves the queue only after it has been saved.

data.name: FmStep5Tech
data.value: A .NET worker service with manual acknowledgements: invalid messages are rejected for good, database failures are retried.

data.name: FmStep6Text
data.value: Every reading is kept together with the time it was measured. History is never deleted, not even when a sensor is switched off or retired.

data.name: FmStep6Tech
data.value: PostgreSQL through Entity Framework Core. A migration service prepares the schema before anything else starts.

data.name: FmStep7Text
data.value: The API is the only way in for apps. It answers questions such as “what are the latest readings in Greenhouse 1?”, and only ever with the customer's own data.

data.name: FmStep7Tech
data.value: ASP.NET Core Minimal APIs. A server-side tenant context and query filters keep every customer's data apart.

data.name: FmStep8Text
data.value: The grower opens the app, picks a location and sees its current values first, then charts of the history.

data.name: FmStep8Tech
data.value: A Blazor web app with MudBlazor. A .NET MAUI mobile app will reuse the same UI components.

data.name: FmDesignIntro
data.value: Pragmatic Clean Architecture in a modular monolith: one codebase, a handful of deployable processes, and business capabilities organised as vertical slices. The diagrams show the target design.

data.name: FmDiagFlowText
data.value: One measurement's way from the hardware to the database. A message leaves the queue only once its data is saved, so a crash never loses it. Invalid input is rejected for good, while database failures are retried.

data.name: FmDiagFlowSource
data.value: sequenceDiagram autonumber participant A as Adapter participant M as MQTT broker participant I as Ingestion participant R as RabbitMQ participant W as Telemetry worker participant DB as PostgreSQL A->>M: publish measurements M->>I: deliver I->>R: publish (persistent) R->>W: deliver, one at a time alt invalid message W->>R: reject, never retried else valid message W->>DB: find the sensor by its external ID alt unknown or disabled sensor W->>R: acknowledge, not stored else active sensor W->>DB: save the reading alt saved W->>R: acknowledge else database error W->>R: requeue and retry end end end

data.name: FmDiagDomainText
data.value: Tenant → Location → Sensor → Reading. There is deliberately no Device entity: hardware is an integration detail, and an external ID links incoming data to a sensor. Every tenant-owned entity carries its own tenant ID, and sensor types are shared reference data.

data.name: FmDiagDomainSource
FmDec1Title
data.value: No Device in the core domain

data.name: FmDec1Text
data.value: Users think in locations and sensors, not in boards. Hardware stays at the integration edge, and an external ID links incoming data to a sensor. New hardware never touches the domain.

data.name: FmDec2Text
data.value: MQTT is the lightweight protocol hardware speaks. RabbitMQ gives the backend durable queues and controlled delivery. Each one serves its own boundary.

data.name: FmDec3Text
data.value: A message leaves the queue only once its readings are stored. Invalid input is rejected, database failures are retried, and a crash never loses data.

data.name: FmDec4Text
data.value: Readings carry no customer ID. The tenant is resolved from the sensor a reading belongs to, and a tenant ID sent by a client or device is never trusted.

data.name: FmDec5Text
data.value: Sensors are disabled or retired, not deleted, and readings are never cascade-deleted. A sensor can't move to another location, so its history always describes the right place.

data.name: FmDec6Text
data.value: Architecture tests check which projects may reference which, and keep hardware terms out of the domain, so the design can't erode silently.
